components.name: Default Button

components.description: Global FTS5 search field in the header.

narrative.overview:
This is an operator's console, not a showroom. Aayush is the only regular viewer, opening it several times a day for a running mental model of where his career pipeline, ventures, projects, outreach, and deadlines stand — and occasionally screen-sharing it, so it has to hold up to a second pair of eyes without needing the density stripped out first. The system is low-lit and unhurried: dark tonal surfaces, one cool accent, a small set of status hues used sparingly, no chrome for its own sake.

The current implementation leans dense and terminal-like — tight paddings, near-uniform micro-typography, color-coded left borders doing most of the hierarchy work. The direction is to move it toward calm, spacious, considered: fewer competing signals, more breathing room, typography (not colored stripes) carrying the weight of hierarchy. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS admin-template look, decorative flourish for its own sake, and cramped layouts that trade breathing room for raw information density.
keyCharacteristics: Three-step tonal surface stack (bg-void → panel → panel-raised) creates depth; no shadows anywhere.
One cool accent (accent) for interaction and focus; four status hues (gold, red, green, violet) each carry one specific meaning, never decorative.
A single sans-serif family at many sizes rather than a distinct display/body pairing — utilitarian, not editorial.
Left-border color coding is the dominant hierarchy device today; the system is moving away from leaning on it as the only signal.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Every status hue (gold, red, green, violet) maps to exactly one semantic meaning across the whole app. Never reuse a status color for a different signal just because it's visually convenient in a new spot.

rules.name: The No Second Bold Rule
rules.body: Weight 700 is reserved for the page title alone. Emphasis elsewhere comes from color or a lighter medium weight (500), never from a second bold size.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are distinguished by background lightness and a hairline border, never by shadow. If a new component needs to feel above the page, move it one step up the tonal stack before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do keep every status hue (gold, red, green, violet) mapped to exactly one meaning app-wide.
Do build new surfaces from the three-step tonal stack before reaching for a shadow.
Do reserve 700 weight for the page title only; use color, size, or 500-weight for everything else.
Do favor more padding and fewer simultaneous signals per component as the system moves toward calm and spacious, even where it costs some density.
Do keep new components legible to a second, screen-sharing viewer — not just skimmable by the builder mid-triage.
donts: Don't ship a generic SaaS admin-template look — no default card-grid dashboard kit aesthetic.
Don't add decorative flourishes for their own sake — no glassmorphism, no gradient accents, nothing ornamental that isn't carrying information.
Don't default to cramped, terminal-dense layouts that trade breathing room for raw information density.
Don't introduce orange decoratively — it's a reserved fifth status hue with no assigned meaning yet.
Don't lean on colored left-borders as the only hierarchy signal on a new component; pair or replace with typographic weight/size once the type scale is revisited.
